summary: Testing SDK hop 2 (55->56) was BLOCKED by a critical, 100%-reproducible Metro build error unrelated to the AppTabBar/useIsFocused changes under test. Backend (/api/health, /api/auth/login) confirmed 200 OK. Frontend: the language-selection screen (first screen) loads cleanly with zero console errors. However, every screen past it (/consent, /(tabs), and presumably all routes that transitively pull in the tabs/consent bundle) immediately renders Metro's red 'Resolution Error' overlay: "Unable to resolve module ./LeafletDestinationMapPicker.web" from src/women/DestinationMapPicker.web.tsx line 43. This is a dangling dynamic import (`lazy(() => import('./LeafletDestinationMapPicker.web'))`) to a file that does not exist anywhere in the repo (confirmed via glob search — no LeafletDestinationMapPicker.web.tsx/.tsx file exists, unlike the analogous ActiveJourneyMap.web.tsx which has no such lazy-Leaflet-fallback at all despite the comment claiming 'same pattern already used'). Reproduced 3 times, including after a full Metro cache clear + supervisor restart (rm -rf .metro-cache + sudo supervisorctl restart expo) — same error every time, so this is not a stale-cache artifact. Because Metro statically analyzes dynamic import() calls at bundle time regardless of the runtime WEB_API_KEY-empty guard around it, this single dangling import breaks the ENTIRE web bundle for any route depending on that chunk, making it impossible to reach login, the home tab, AppTabBar, or any of the Head Out / SOS / Evidence Vault / admin-issues regression screens requested in this test pass. Per `git status`, src/women/DestinationMapPicker.web.tsx is a locally modified (uncommitted) file with this broken lazy-import added, along with a 'followUserKey'/'mapHeight' refactor — this looks like leftover/incomplete work from a different (Google-Maps-fallback) feature, not part of the SDK-56 hop's described changes (app/(tabs)/index.tsx useIsFocused swap and AppTabBar.tsx local type), but it is currently blocking all verification of those two changes.

critical_code_review_comments: DestinationMapPicker.web.tsx comment at line 40-42 claims 'same pattern already used' as ActiveJourneyMap.web.tsx, but ActiveJourneyMap.web.tsx (viewed directly) has no Leaflet/lazy-import fallback at all — it's a plain Google-Maps-only component. The comment is misleading/inaccurate and the referenced pattern doesn't actually exist yet, which suggests this was mid-refactor when left in this state.

Static dynamic import() targets in Metro/webpack bundlers are always resolved at build time for the dependency graph even though they execute lazily at runtime — a dangling lazy-import target is exactly as fatal as a dangling static import, just with a slightly different error surface (Resolution Error overlay vs. immediate throw). This should be caught by any `expo export`/typecheck/build-time smoke check before being left in the tree.

git status shows this file (along with DestinationMapPicker.tsx, DestinationPicker.tsx, useJourneyGPS.ts, mapValidation.ts, head-out.tsx, nearest-help.tsx) all locally modified and ActiveJourneyMap.tsx/.web.tsx newly added — none of this matches the problem statement's description of 'only 2 files changed for this SDK hop' (app/(tabs)/index.tsx and AppTabBar.tsx), suggesting unrelated in-progress work is currently committed to the working tree alongside the SDK hop's actual changes and should be separated/stabilized before continuing the SDK upgrade chain.

rca_of_issue: root cause: src/women/DestinationMapPicker.web.tsx line 43 declares `const LeafletDestinationMapPicker = lazy(() => import('./LeafletDestinationMapPicker.web'));` but no file named LeafletDestinationMapPicker.web.tsx (or .ts/.jsx) exists anywhere under /app/frontend (confirmed via glob_files '**/LeafletDestinationMapPicker*' returning zero matches). Metro's bundler statically resolves all import()/require() targets — including inside lazy() — while building the module graph for a given route chunk, independent of whether the runtime code path that would actually execute the import is reached. Because this component is reachable from the app's root layout/tabs stack (the DestinationPicker/Head Out feature is wired into shared navigation), the broken import poisons the whole bundle for /consent, /(tabs), and every other route tested, while leaving the standalone /language route (bundled separately/earlier, before this dependency is pulled in) unaffected. Mitigation: either implement the missing LeafletDestinationMapPicker.web.tsx (a react-leaflet component accepting markerPos/radiusMeters/onPositionChange/recenterKey/mapHeight props, mirroring DestinationMapPicker's Google Maps branch) or remove/revert the lazy-import addition and restore the previous plain 'Map unavailable — web API key not configured' fallback text until that component is ready.
